title: The Off-Grid Survival Manual: Step-by-Step DIY Projects for Water, Food, Power, Shelter &
description: The next blackout is coming. This time, have a plan that's already built. An ice storm takes the power for six days. The taps slow to a trickle, the freezer starts to thaw, and the space heater you were counting on is a paperweight. If that scenario keeps you up at night, this is the book that fixes it — not more theory, and not fear for its own sake, but a stack of real projects you can build on a weekend with tools you already own. The Off-Grid Survival Manual is a hands-on build guide for keeping a household running when the usual supply quits. Every project comes with a plain materials list (real sizes, gauges, and fuse ratings), numbered steps, an honest time-and-cost estimate, and a clear black-and-white diagram you can actually build from. No filler. No wall of half-explained ideas you'll never start. You'll build working systems across the five that matter most: Water — rainwater catchment, gravity filters, a solar still, and greywater reuse, so the taps stopping doesn't stop you. Power — size a solar array, wire a 12-volt battery bank safely, and add wind or micro-hydro, with the electrical done right. Food — raised beds, a chicken coop, aquaponics, seed saving, and a solar dehydrator that keep food on the table. Shelter & Heat — a rocket mass heater, a root cellar, and building methods that hold warmth when the furnace won't. Security — a simple family plan and a defensible layout that protect your home without turning it into a bunker. Plus the readiness foundation that ties it together: a family emergency plan, first aid, and off-grid communication. It's written for the capable beginner — the handy homeowner, the weekend builder, the parent who would rather own three things that work than thirty that don't. title: The Off-Grid Survival Projects Handbook, Volume 2: 69 Step-by-Step Projects for Cold Night
description: When the power goes out on a cold night, do you know how to keep the heat in, the water safe, and your family fed? Most survival books start with the big builds. The first bad night does not wait for them. The Off-Grid Survival Projects Handbook, Volume 2 gives you 69 step-by-step projects, ordered the way trouble arrives: first night first, then outward. Most are laid out the same clear way, so you always know what to gather, what it costs, and exactly what to do. Most projects include: A difficulty, time, and cost label up front, so you can pick work that fits your day and your budget A "You will need" list A Safety block that comes before the steps Numbered steps you can follow A labeled diagram so you can see how it goes together Troubleshooting for when something goes wrong, and a Level Up note for when you have the basics Inside you will build the skills that matter most: The first bad night: a utility shutoff station, battery carbon monoxide alarms, fire prevention, downed power lines and flood water, and frozen pipes Heat: heating one room safely, a cold-weather sleep system, window insulation, a chimney and stovepipe inspection, and a rocket mass heater bench Water: hauling, storing, and treating drinking water, a barrel sand and gravel filter, a solar still, a hydraulic ram pump, and a spring box Food: a hay box, sourdough without a fridge, a 3-month pantry, dried food and jerky, dry-pack jars, and a no-power ice box Skills, tools, and land: map and compass, a Stop the Bleed wound kit, a 12-volt battery box, salvage, keeping an edge, a brake-drum forge, grafting, shiitake logs, and a living hedge and windbreak You also get a Scenario Index that sends you to the right projects when a pipe freezes, the water is not safe, the fridge goes off, or a storm is coming

description: You can stockpile all the rice you like... but do you know how you're going to cook it if you're without power for months on end? Once upon a time, disaster preparedness was a fairly niche pastime. Today, it’s becoming mainstream… and you only have to look at the headlines to see why. Extreme weather events… global pandemics… growing unrest… All of these factors are in your consciousness all the time. It makes sense to be prepared for the worst… and with celebrities like Ryan Seacrest and Ronda Rousey joining the ranks, more and more people are beginning to understand why. But despite this growing trend, there’s one thing most people are missing. You’ve stocked your pantry; you have enough toilet roll to see you through the next few months; you have your bug out bag prepped… But have you thought about what you’re going to do if the grid goes down? If the power grid fails, it’s not just your lights that go out. It’s your water supply. It’s your heating and cooling system. It’s all your usual ways of cooking food or doing the laundry. Without the grid, life as we know it changes in an instant. Are you prepared for that? Don’t panic. If your emergency preparedness plan has a few holes in it just now, you’re in the right place. title: EMP No Grid No Warning: An EMP Post Apocalypse Prepper Survival Thriller
description: Overnight, an EMP sent America back to the age before electricity. Her promise didn't age a day Years ago, they took away her wings. Yesterday, the EMP took down her plane. Grace appeared to be just another grandmother on a crowded flight. Then the EMP killed the engines, and the pilots didn't make it. Now the only survivor who knows how to keep a child alive in a frozen mountain range is an old woman the world forgot was ever a pilot at all. There's no rescue coming. No working grid. No government riding in to help. Nothing but miles of lawless, empty country between a stranded child and her family's front gate. And one woman who's done being forgotten.
